pageConvention: PDF physical page index, starting at 1
evaluation: Manual model QA: judge answer meaning and original evidence, not exact wording. referencePages are starting points, not an exhaustive whitelist. minimumDistinctEvidencePages applies to the answer's supporting citations.

cases.question: According to the paper, why should a new key pair be used for each transaction? Does this prevent all transaction linking? Cite the original text.
expectedPoints: New key pairs reduce linking transactions to a common owner.
Multi-input transactions still reveal common ownership; complete unlinkability is not guaranteed.

cases.question: Using the Introduction, Proof-of-Work, and Conclusion sections, explain how proof-of-work helps prevent double-spending and what security assumption it relies on. Cite at least two of these sections.
expectedPoints: Proof-of-work establishes a verifiable, chronologically ordered transaction history.
Changing history requires redoing the affected block and all subsequent work.
Security depends on honest nodes controlling more CPU power than cooperating attackers, rather than a majority of nodes.

cases.question: Does this paper provide Satoshi Nakamoto's real name and home address? Answer using only the document.
cases.expectedBehavior: State that the document does not provide a verified real name or home address. Do not guess or treat the author byline, email or website as identity evidence. For partial input, limit the absence claim to the supplied excerpts.

cases.question: How many layers do the encoder and decoder each have? What are the model dimension and the inner dimension of the feed-forward network? Cite both the architecture and feed-forward network descriptions.
expectedPoints: The encoder and decoder each have 6 layers.
The model dimension is d_model = 512.
The feed-forward network inner dimension is d_ff = 2048.

cases.question: What BLEU scores does the abstract report for WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation? Keep each score paired with the correct task and cite the text.
expectedPoints: WMT 2014 English-to-German: 28.4 BLEU.
WMT 2014 English-to-French: 41.8 BLEU.

cases.question: Does this paper report the time to first token for Gemma 4 E4B in the current browser application? Answer using only the document.
cases.expectedBehavior: State that the document does not report this browser deployment's time to first token. Do not substitute training time, GPU count or other benchmark results. For partial input, limit the absence claim to the supplied excerpts.

cases.question: Directly inspect Figure 1 and list the start point, end point, and color of every arrow. Do not infer them from the body text.
cases.expectedBehavior: Disclose that only extracted text is available and that graphical connections and colors cannot be inspected reliably. The figure can be located on PDF page 3, but a caption does not establish visual inspection.

cases.question: What are the GFS chunk size and the initial lease timeout? How can a lease be extended? Cite the original evidence for each.
expectedPoints: Chunks are 64 MB.
The initial lease timeout is 60 seconds.
While a chunk is being mutated, the primary can request and typically receive extensions from the master.

cases.question: Must file data pass through the master when a client reads a file? What are the roles of the master and the chunkservers? Cite the paper.
expectedPoints: The master provides metadata, chunk handles and replica locations.
Clients read file data directly from chunkservers.
A single master does not mean that all file data passes through it.

cases.question: Does this paper provide a complete open-source repository URL and software installation commands for GFS? Use only the document.
cases.expectedBehavior: State that the document does not provide a complete open-source repository URL or installation commands for GFS. Do not invent instructions or substitute HDFS documentation. For partial input, limit the absence claim to the supplied excerpts.

cases.question: Why must completed map tasks be re-executed after a worker failure, while completed reduce tasks do not need to be re-executed? Explain the difference in output storage and cite the paper.
expectedPoints: Map output is on the failed worker's local disks and becomes inaccessible.
Reduce output is stored in a global file system.
Do not claim that all completed tasks need to be re-executed.

cases.question: Compare task re-execution after worker failures with backup tasks near the end of a MapReduce job. What problem does each mechanism solve? Cite evidence from both sections.
expectedPoints: Failure recovery reschedules lost or unfinished work.
Backup tasks mitigate stragglers that delay job completion.
Both mechanisms re-execute tasks, but they have different triggers.

cases.question: Does this paper report the system's memory usage and inference speed in Chrome WebGPU? Answer using only the document.
cases.expectedBehavior: State that the document does not report browser WebGPU memory usage or inference speed. Do not substitute cluster throughput or job duration. For partial input, limit the absence claim to the supplied excerpts.

cases.question: How do randomized election timeouts reduce split votes in Raft? What example interval does the paper give, and is that interval mandatory for every deployment? Cite the text.
expectedPoints: Randomized timeouts spread out election starts and reduce repeated split votes.
The example interval is 150-300 ms.
The interval is an example rather than a mandatory parameter for every deployment.

cases.question: How does the majority requirement for a normal leader election differ from the requirement during joint consensus? Why is the joint-consensus requirement needed during a configuration change? Cite both parts of the paper.
expectedPoints: Normal elections require votes from a majority of the current cluster.
Joint consensus requires separate majorities of both old and new configurations.
This prevents two configurations from making independent decisions during a transition.

cases.question: Does this paper give a formal ISO standard number for the Raft algorithm? Use only the document.
cases.expectedBehavior: State that the document does not provide a formal ISO standard number for Raft. Do not invent one or mistake a section or bibliography number for a standard. For partial input, limit the absence claim to the supplied excerpts.

cases.question: Inspect Figure 6 and describe the exact color and two-dimensional position of every box. Do not supplement the answer with body text.
cases.expectedBehavior: Disclose that text input cannot directly reveal figure colors or exact two-dimensional positions. The figure can be located on PDF page 6. Do not present body text or an extracted caption as visual observation.
